organization.CNS: brain + spinal cord. integration + command center.
organization.PNS: everything outside CNS. cranial nerves (12 pairs) + spinal nerves (31 pairs) + ganglia.
organization.sensory_afferent: signals FROM receptors TO CNS. somatic (body wall) + visceral (organs).
organization.motor_efferent: signals FROM CNS TO effectors. two divisions:
organization.somatic_nervous_system: voluntary. motor neurons → skeletal muscle. ONE neuron pathway.
organization.autonomic_nervous_system: involuntary. two-neuron chain → smooth muscle, cardiac muscle, glands.

cell_body_soma.what: contains nucleus, organelles (rough ER = nissl bodies, mitochondria, golgi). the metabolic center.
cell_body_soma.nissl_bodies: clusters of rough ER. prominent in neurons. protein synthesis. unique to neuron cell bodies.

histology_neurons.dendrites: SHORT branching extensions. RECEIVE signals. the 'antennae.' increase surface area for input.

axon.what: LONG single process. CONDUCTS action potentials AWAY from cell body. one per neuron.
axon.axon_hillock: cone-shaped area where axon emerges from soma. TRIGGER ZONE — where AP is initiated if threshold is reached.
axon.axon_terminals: branched endings. contain SYNAPTIC VESICLES with neurotransmitter.
axon.myelin_sheath: lipid-rich insulating layer around axon. speeds conduction. formed by SCHWANN CELLS (PNS) or OLIGODENDROCYTES (CNS).
axon.nodes_of_ranvier: gaps in myelin between adjacent schwann cells/oligo segments. where ion channels cluster. AP 'jumps' between nodes = SALTATORY CONDUCTION.
axon.white_matter: myelinated axon tracts. looks white because of myelin lipid.
axon.gray_matter: cell bodies, dendrites, unmyelinated axons. processing areas.

structural_types.multipolar: 1 axon + many dendrites. MOST COMMON. motor neurons, interneurons.
structural_types.bipolar: 1 axon + 1 dendrite. RARE. retina, olfactory epithelium, inner ear.
structural_types.unipolar_pseudounipolar: single process splits into peripheral + central branch. sensory neurons in dorsal root ganglia. the 'T-shape.'

functional_types.sensory_afferent: carry impulses FROM receptors TO CNS.
functional_types.motor_efferent: carry impulses FROM CNS TO effectors (muscles, glands).
functional_types.interneurons_association: BETWEEN sensory and motor. integration. 99% of all neurons. CNS only.

neuroglia.note: supporting cells. do NOT conduct impulses. CAN divide (unlike neurons). outnumber neurons ~10:1.

functions: blood-brain barrier (BBB) — cover capillaries with feet, control what enters brain
recycle neurotransmitters (uptake glutamate → convert to glutamine → give back to neuron)

oligodendrocytes.function: MYELINATE axons in CNS. one oligo wraps segments of MULTIPLE axons (unlike schwann which wraps one).
oligodendrocytes.note: CNS myelin doesn't regenerate well. that's why spinal cord injuries are devastating.

microglia.function: immune defense of CNS. PHAGOCYTIC. derived from monocytes. activated by infection/injury. brain's macrophages.

ependymal_cells.function: line ventricles + central canal of spinal cord. produce + circulate CSF. some have cilia that move CSF.

schwann_cells.function: MYELINATE axons in PNS. ONE schwann cell wraps ONE segment of ONE axon. key difference from oligos.
schwann_cells.regeneration: schwann cells form a REGENERATION TUBE after peripheral nerve injury → axon can regrow through it. PNS regenerates, CNS doesn't.

satellite_cells.function: surround neuron cell bodies in GANGLIA. support + regulate environment. PNS equivalent of astrocytes (loosely).

resting_potential.maintained_by: Na+/K+ ATPase pump: pumps 3 Na+ OUT, 2 K+ IN per ATP. net export of positive charge.
resting_potential.ion_distribution: Na+ HIGH outside, LOW inside. K+ HIGH inside, LOW outside. at rest: K+ leak channels are open (more permeable to K+). K+ leaks out → makes inside more negative.
resting_potential.polarized: cell at resting potential is POLARIZED (charge difference across membrane).

graded_potentials.what: small LOCAL changes in membrane potential. vary in magnitude. DECREASE with distance (decremental). not self-propagating.

types.EPSP: excitatory postsynaptic potential. depolarization (closer to threshold). Na+ entering.
types.IPSP: inhibitory postsynaptic potential. hyperpolarization (farther from threshold). Cl- entering or K+ leaving.

summation.temporal: rapid-fire signals from SAME synapse add up.
summation.spatial: signals from MULTIPLE synapses at same time add up.

action_potential.what: all-or-nothing electrical signal. self-propagating. does NOT decrease with distance. nerve impulse.
action_potential.threshold: ~-55mV. must reach this to fire. below = nothing. at/above = FULL AP.

phases.1_resting: -70mV. voltage-gated Na+ and K+ channels closed.
phases.2_depolarization: stimulus reaches threshold → VOLTAGE-GATED Na+ CHANNELS OPEN → Na+ rushes IN → membrane goes positive → peaks at +30mV.
phases.3_repolarization: Na+ channels INACTIVATE (not just close — different conformational state). VOLTAGE-GATED K+ CHANNELS OPEN (delayed) → K+ rushes OUT → membrane returns toward negative.
phases.4_hyperpolarization: K+ channels slow to close → membrane overshoots past -70mV to about -80mV briefly. then K+ channels close.
phases.5_return_to_resting: Na+/K+ pump restores ion gradients. Na+ channels reset from inactivated → closed (ready to open again).

refractory_periods.absolute: during depolarization + early repolarization. Na+ channels are INACTIVATED — CANNOT open regardless of stimulus strength. ensures one-way propagation + limits firing rate.
refractory_periods.relative: during late repolarization + hyperpolarization. K+ channels still open. a STRONGER-THAN-NORMAL stimulus CAN trigger another AP.

propagation.continuous: in UNMYELINATED fibers. AP generated at every point along membrane. slow (0.5-2 m/s).
propagation.saltatory: in MYELINATED fibers. AP jumps from node to node (nodes of Ranvier). fast (up to 120 m/s). more energy efficient.

synapses.electrical_synapses: gap junctions. direct ion flow between cells. FAST. bidirectional. cardiac muscle, some smooth muscle, some CNS neurons.

chemical_synapses.components: presynaptic terminal → synaptic cleft (20-50nm gap) → postsynaptic membrane
sequence: 2. voltage-gated Ca2+ channels open → Ca2+ enters terminal
3. Ca2+ causes synaptic vesicles to fuse with presynaptic membrane (EXOCYTOSIS)
5. NT crosses cleft, binds RECEPTORS on postsynaptic membrane
6. receptor activation opens ion channels → EPSP or IPSP
7. NT removed by: REUPTAKE (back into presynaptic), ENZYMATIC DEGRADATION (AChE breaks ACh), or DIFFUSION away

neurotransmitters.acetylcholine_ACh: NMJ (skeletal muscle), parasympathetic. excitatory at NMJ. degraded by AChE.
neurotransmitters.dopamine: pleasure, reward, motor control. deficiency → Parkinson's. excess → schizophrenia.
neurotransmitters.serotonin: mood, sleep, appetite. target of SSRIs (antidepressants).
neurotransmitters.GABA: main INHIBITORY NT of CNS. target of benzodiazepines, alcohol, barbiturates.
neurotransmitters.glutamate: main EXCITATORY NT of CNS. learning + memory. excess → excitotoxicity.
neurotransmitters.endorphins: natural painkillers. bind opioid receptors. runner's high.

neural_integration.serial_processing: one neuron to the next in a chain. reflexes. predictable.
neural_integration.parallel_processing: multiple pathways process same info simultaneously. higher brain functions. thinking.
neural_integration.convergence: MANY presynaptic neurons → ONE postsynaptic neuron. input from multiple sources.
neural_integration.divergence: ONE presynaptic neuron → MANY postsynaptic neurons. one signal spreads to many targets.

clinical.multiple_sclerosis: autoimmune destruction of CNS myelin. demyelination → slowed/blocked conduction. relapsing-remitting pattern.
clinical.guillain_barre: autoimmune attack on PNS myelin (schwann cells). ascending paralysis. can recover because PNS regenerates.
clinical.parkinsons: loss of dopamine-producing neurons in substantia nigra. tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia.
clinical.local_anesthetics: block voltage-gated Na+ channels → prevent AP generation. no pain signal.
clinical.nerve_gas_organophosphates: inhibit AChE → ACh not degraded → continuous stimulation → paralysis, death.
